item.title: Autonomous Frameworks ScientistTwo and CDA Advance Enterprise Model Discovery and Scientific Research
item.description:
Autonomous Frameworks ScientistTwo and CDA Advance Enterprise Model Discovery and Scientific Research

Researchers have announced developments in autonomous discovery with the introduction of ScientistTwo and the Continual Discovery Agent (CDA). ScientistTwo is a multi-agent framework designed to automate the scientific research cycle, while CDA focuses on discovering and revising world models within enterprise systems. These developments aim to create agents that can learn complex rules and generate expert-level outputs without human intervention.

🔍 Overview

The research focuses on two primary systems designed for autonomous learning and discovery:

  • ScientistTwo: A fully autonomous multi-agent framework that establishes baselines, formulates hypotheses, and coordinates specialized agents for end-to-end research cycles.
  • Continual Discovery Agent (CDA): An agent that starts without knowledge of business rules in an enterprise system and discovers them by interacting with records and observing outcomes.

🧩 How it works

ScientistTwo utilizes a closed-loop system to manage scientific tasks:

  • Takes an initial problem as input and coordinates specialized agents to orchestrate an end-to-end discovery cycle.
  • Conducts experiments using diverse datasets and metrics.
  • Refines methodologies through automated ablation studies.
  • Validates findings via a closed-loop simulated peer-review rebuttal engine.

CDA operates within enterprise environments to build and maintain world models:

  • Observes effects where updating one field can set another, create a record, or start an approval.
  • Builds a world model from observations and revises it as rules change.
  • Predicts the effects of hidden rules without querying the running system.

⚙️ Key details

To evaluate these systems, researchers established specific benchmarks and environments:

Component Detail
EnterpriseWorldShift A live ServiceNow environment with nine tables and 25 hidden rules.
Evaluation Actions 600 actions used to test discovery, revision, extension, and retirement.
Performance Metric CDA predicts hidden rule effects up to 8.98 IoU points more accurately than lookup-based approaches.
Scientific Benchmarks ScientistTwo is tested against papers from conferences such as ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS.

💡 Why it matters

ScientistTwo produces expert-level, publishable papers and fully verified, executable codebases. Its solutions consistently outperform human state-of-the-art models and achieve higher average review ratings than human-authored papers when evaluated by automated AI review agents. In enterprise contexts, CDA demonstrates the ability to carry a learned world model across different versions of a system, accurately predicting the effects of business rules that are revised, added, or removed over time.

#AIAgents #MachineLearning #ScientistTwo #EnterpriseSoftware #AutonomousDiscovery

Source: Continual Enterprise World Model Discovery in Dynamic Systems Source: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI

item.title: Introduction of ERPBench for Evaluating Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Systems
item.description:
Introduction of ERPBench for Evaluating Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Systems

Researchers have introduced ERPBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate screenshot-only AI agents operating within live Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. This development addresses the gap between general desktop task evaluation and the specific complexities of enterprise software.

🔍 Overview

ERP systems manage finance, procurement, inventory, and customer operations globally. They present distinct challenges for computer-use agents, including:

  • Dense interfaces
  • Coordinated multi-step interactions
  • Errors that alter persistent business records rather than appearing on screen

⚙️ Key details

Unlike existing enterprise benchmarks that use simulated approximations or proprietary platforms, ERPBench utilizes a live and reproducible ERP system. Key features include:

  • Database Scoring: Tasks are scored against ground-truth values stored in the database.
  • Production-Grade Harness: A system that gates agent actions behind human approval for safe deployment, though ERPBench itself runs autonomously.

💡 Why it matters

Evaluation of six closed and open-source agents revealed that strong general GUI performance does not transfer to enterprise reliability. Findings include:

  • Agents frequently save records that contain incorrect values.
  • In some runs, agents successfully save in up to 85% of instances, but write the correct value in as few as 3% of those runs.
  • The benchmark allows for the characterization of failure modes specific to enterprise workflows.

#ERPBench #AIagents #EnterpriseSoftware #GUIagents #Benchmarks

Source: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software Source: TuiML: Machine Learning for AI Agents Source: RideWay: Benchmarking Efficient Task Completion for Tool-Using Language Agents Source: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents

item.title: Certinia Expands Veda Suite With 14 Autonomous Agents and 135 Tools
item.description:
Certinia Expands Veda Suite With 14 Autonomous Agents and 135 Tools

Certinia has expanded its Veda suite by adding 14 autonomous agents and expanding its Intelligent Actions library to 135 tools.

🧩 How it works

The platform connects and coordinates key processes across the enterprise lifecycle by performing the following actions:

  • Workflow Coordination: It coordinates professional services, customer success, and accounting processes.
  • General Ledger Actions: It executes general ledger actions through Model Context Protocol connections.

⚙️ Key details

The expansion introduces several key updates to the platform’s automation capabilities:

  • Autonomous Agents: The suite now includes 14 new autonomous agents.
  • Intelligent Actions: The system’s tool library has been expanded to a total of 135 tools.
  • Operational Reach: The tools span professional services, customer success, and accounting workflows.

#Certinia #AIagents #EnterpriseSoftware

item.title: Boomi Introduces Boomi Scribe AI Agent for Automated Integration Documentation
item.description:
Boomi Introduces Boomi Scribe AI Agent for Automated Integration Documentation

Boomi has developed Boomi Scribe, an AI-powered agent running on AWS designed to automate and streamline the documentation process for enterprise development teams.

💡 Why it matters

Enterprise developers often struggle to maintain documentation for workflows involving integrations across multiple applications and data sources. This presents several challenges:

  • Technical Debt: Documentation is a persistent source of technical debt for enterprise teams.
  • Readability: Without accurate documentation, workflows can be unreadable to anyone other than the original creator, complicating debugging and handoffs.
  • Operational Risks: Manual documentation is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, which can lead to rework, lost time, and gaps in auditing for compliance needs.
  • Version Control: Comparing changes between process versions manually is tedious and error-prone.

🧩 How it works

Boomi Scribe uses a multi-step approach to transform technical metadata into user-friendly documentation:

  1. Parsing: The agent parses XML files containing integration process metadata to extract relevant features.
  2. Transformation: These features are converted into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) dot notation format, representing the workflow as nodes and edges.
  3. Generation: The parsed DAG is passed to AI models via Amazon Bedrock to generate natural language documentation.
  4. Comparison: The agent compares different versions of DAGs to highlight component differences and changes.
  5. Storage: The results are stored in Amazon S3.

⚙️ Key details

Boomi Scribe leverages several AWS services and AI models to function:

Component Purpose
Claude Haiku 4.5 A few-shot learning model used to process DAGs and generate natural language documentation and summaries.
Amazon Bedrock Provides the foundational LLMs used for documentation generation.
Amazon SageMaker AI Used to build and maintain models for classifying user intents.
AWS Lambda Orchestrates the entire pipeline from parsing to comparison.
Amazon S3 Stores DAG files, generated documentation, and metadata.
Amazon DynamoDB Serves as the internal backend datastore for service operations.

🔍 Overview

The generated documentation includes the following sections:

  • High-level Overview: A summary of the workflow for stakeholders and a process diagram.
  • Process Metadata: Details including name, version, dates, paths, and the number of steps and components.
  • Business Context: Information regarding the purpose of the process.
  • Process Steps and Functions: Concise, step-by-step descriptions for each workflow step.

This documentation and metadata are available for contextual reference within Boomi GPT and the Boomi Integration Canvas.

#Boomi #AWS #AmazonBedrock #AIagents #EnterpriseSoftware

Source: How Boomi Scribe streamlines documentation using AWS | Amazon Web Services
